problem: Let $A(-1,3,2,-4)$, $B(1,0,1,-2)$, and $C(0,1,-1,2).$ Find the cosine of the angle $∠BAC.$
worked_solution:
Let $v=\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $w=\overset{\to }{AC}.$ Then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =b-a \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -3 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

and

$$
\begin{aligned}w & =c-a \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ -3 \\ 6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

Let $\theta =m∠BAC$ be the angle between the vectors $v$ and $w.$ Then, we can find $\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ using the following formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{v\cdot w}{‖v‖\,‖w‖} \\  & =\frac{{v}_{1}{w}_{1}+{v}_{2}{w}_{2}+{v}_{3}{w}_{3}+{v}_{4}{w}_{4}}{\sqrt{{v}_{1}^{2}+{v}_{2}^{2}+{v}_{3}^{2}+{v}_{4}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{w}_{1}^{2}+{w}_{2}^{2}+{w}_{3}^{2}+{w}_{4}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 1+(-3)\cdot (-2)+(-1)\cdot (-3)+2\cdot 6}{\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}}\,\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{6}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{23}{\sqrt{18}\cdot \sqrt{50}} \\  & =\frac{23}{30}\end{aligned}
$$
